title: Administrative Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations, Department of Medicine
text:
Department Overview:

The Department of Medicine (DoM) at OHSU is comprised of a diverse community of faculty, staff, clinicians, researchers, educators, and learners dedicated to advancing patient care, education, and research across ten divisions.

The Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, quality management, and performance improvement support for inpatient clinical services across the Department of Medicine's ten specialty divisions and care sites. Reporting to the Vice Chair of Clinical Practice and partnering closely with the Vice Chair for Administration, this position serves as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and clinical effectiveness initiatives.

Function/Duties of Position:

Working collaboratively with DoM and OHSU Health quality leaders, division leadership, hospital operations, finance, revenue cycle, informatics, care management, nursing leadership, clinical documentation teams, and physician leaders, the Director advances the Department's inpatient quality, operational, clinical, and financial goals through the design, implementation, and oversight of standardized processes, performance improvement efforts, operational reporting, and strategic initiatives.

Emphasis is placed on quality programing and outcomes, patient safety, clinical documentation integrity, coding accuracy, revenue cycle performance, operational efficiency, provider productivity, inpatient capacity management, and growth planning across all Department of Medicine inpatient services. The Director supports a broad portfolio of inpatient programs spanning multiple clinical specialties and care settings.

This position functions within a highly matrixed environment and serves as a key liaison between departmental leadership and enterprise partners, ensuring alignment with OHSU Health strategic priorities, quality objectives, and high-reliability organizational principles.

**Inpatient Quality and Operations Leadership and Oversight**

* Work in direct partnership with the DoM Vice Chair of Clinical Practice, DoM Associate Vice Chair of Inpatient Services, Healthcare quality leaders, and other institutional leaders to oversee and coordinate quality-focused inpatient care across Department of Medicine divisions.
* Provide strategic administrative leadership and operational oversight for Department of Medicine inpatient programs and services.
* Serve as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and performance improvement initiatives.
* Partner with division heads, section heads, medical directors, healthcare administrators, quality leaders, and physician leaders to identify and address operational and quality barriers affecting patient safety, access, efficiency, provider experience, and clinical outcomes.
* Shape and implement standardized inpatient quality, safety, and operational best practices across medicine specialties.
* Coordinate departmental quality improvement initiatives focused on reducing medical errors, serious safety events, healthcare-associated infections, hospital-acquired conditions, avoidable readmissions, preventable complications, and patient harm.
* Lead administrative efforts related to inpatient quality programs, patient safety activities, inpatient capacity management, patient flow, consult services, discharge efficiency, care coordination, and service-line optimization.
* Support departmental participation in mortality reviews, safety event reviews, quality committees, accreditation activities, regulatory preparedness efforts, and institutional quality initiatives.
* Establish and maintain departmental quality and operational governance structures, including scorecards, dashboards, performance reviews, and accountability processes.
* Partner with healthcare quality teams to identify opportunities for improvement and coordinate development of corrective action plans.
* Serve as the primary administrative liaison between Department of Medicine leadership, inpatient programs, Healthcare quality teams, and hospital operations leadership.
* Monitor operational, quality, and patient safety performance measures and drive action planning to improve outcomes.
* Facilitate multidisciplinary teams and stakeholder groups responsible for advancing inpatient quality, safety, throughput, and operational effectiveness.

**Revenue Cycle, Billing, Coding, and Clinical Documentation Integrity**

* Serve as the Department's operational lead for inpatient professional revenue cycle performance.
* Partner with Revenue Cycle, Professional Coding, Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI), Finance, Compliance, and physician leaders to improve revenue capture, reimbursement, and operational performance.
* Evaluate and improve inpatient provider documentation practices, coding accuracy, charge capture processes, and billing workflows.
* Lead provider education efforts related to documentation requirements, coding regulations, payer expectations, reimbursement methodologies, and compliance standards.
* Monitor inpatient professional fee performance, wRVU generation, Case Mix Index (CMI), coding trends, denials, reimbursement outcomes, and documentation quality measures.
* Develop dashboards and performance reporting tools that support transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Identify specialty-specific opportunities for revenue optimization, operational efficiency, and documentation improvement.

**Performance Improvement and Strategic Initiatives**

* Lead complex inpatient operational and quality improvement initiatives utilizing Lean, process improvement, project management, and change management methodologies.
* Design and implement department-wide initiatives focused on improving quality outcomes, patient safety, throughput, provider experience, financial performance, and operational consistency.
* Conduct workflow analyses and redesign efforts to eliminate inefficiencies, reduce variation in care delivery, and improve service performance.
* Collaborate with Quality, Analytics, Finance, Informatics, and Operations teams to establish measurable goals and monitor outcomes.
* Develop project charters, implementation plans, success metrics, and performance benchmarks for strategic initiatives.
* Support departmental strategic planning activities and implementation of enterprise priorities related to inpatient growth, quality, and operational excellence.
* Advance high-reliability organization principles and support compliance with accreditation and regulatory requirements.

**Data Analytics, Reporting, and Financial Performance**

* Develop and maintain operational, financial, quality, patient safety, and utilization reporting structures for departmental and divisional leadership.
* Establish and maintain comprehensive inpatient quality scorecards and dashboards.
* Monitor and analyze key performance indicators including:
 + Analyze trends in inpatient volumes, utilization, consult activity, throughput, revenue cycle performance, patient outcomes, and quality metrics.
 + Translate complex operational and quality data into actionable recommendations for leaders.
 + Benchmark Department performance against institutional, regional, and national metrics when available.
 + Support financial forecasting, business case development, and investment planning for inpatient growth initiatives.

**Stakeholder Engagement and Committee Leadership**

* Represent the Department of Medicine on institutional committees related to quality, patient safety, inpatient operations, revenue cycle, clinical documentation, care management, patient flow, and performance improvement.
* Build collaborative partnerships with hospital administrators, nursing leaders, physicians, quality teams, informatics, finance, and operational stakeholders.
* Provide subject matter expertise regarding inpatient quality, safety, operational performance, workflow redesign, and professional revenue optimization.
* Lead communication, stakeholder engagement, and change management activities for major inpatient initiatives.
* Support development of a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, patient safety, and operational excellence throughout Department of Medicine inpatient programs.

Required Qualifications:

**Education**

Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, finance, or a related field is required. Master’s degree may substitute for one (1) year of experience.

**Experience**

* Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in clinical operations or healthcare administration, with at least two (2) years in a formal leadership role.
* Experience supporting inpatient hospital operations, quality improvement, patient safety, healthcare finance, revenue cycle, or operational excellence initiatives.
* Experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives within healthcare organizations.
* Experience working collaboratively with physician leaders, nursing leadership, and hospital operational teams.
* Experience developing performance metrics, scorecards, dashboards, and operational improvement plans.

**Competencies**

* Strong knowledge of inpatient healthcare operations and physician practice management.
* Strong knowledge of healthcare quality improvement, patient safety, performance measurement, and high-reliability organizational principles.
* Knowledge of inpatient reimbursement methodologies, documentation requirements, clinical coding, and revenue cycle practices.
* Knowledge of regulatory, accreditation, and quality reporting requirements affecting inpatient healthcare delivery.
* Advanced analytical, reporting, and data interpretation skills.
* Demonstrated ability to develop quality scorecards, operational dashboards, and executive-level performance reporting.
* Ability to analyze complex clinical, operational, financial, and quality data and translate findings into actionable improvement strategies.
* Demonstrated ability to manage large-scale operational and performance improvement initiatives across multiple clinical specialties.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary efforts focused on reducing medical errors, improving patient outcomes, and advancing a culture of safety.
* Excellent communication, facilitation, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
* Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes without direct authority.
* Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, Epic, reporting platforms, and healthcare analytics tools.
* Strong financial acumen, strategic planning, and business case development capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications:

**Education**

Master’s Degree in Health Care Administration, Business, Public Health or Nursing; or Bachelor’s degree with equivalent combination of education, experience and training.

**Experience**

* Eight or more years of progressively responsible healthcare operations, quality, or performance improvement experience.
* Academic medical center experience.
* Experience with inpatient physician billing and professional fee revenue cycle.
* Experience with quality reporting, patient safety programs, accreditation activities, and regulatory readiness.
* Experience with Epic reporting, provider productivity analysis, CDI initiatives, and coding optimization.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or process improvement certification or training.
* Matrix leadership experience.

**Competencies**

Demonstrated ability to leverage advanced analytics, financial modeling, forecasting tools, artificial intelligence-enabled technologies, and other data-driven methodologies to improve operational efficiency, inform strategic decision-making, optimize resource allocation, and support sustainable program growth.

Additional Details:

Professional office environment; may include occasional travel to affiliate and partner sites. In-person work schedule expected, with limited telework acceptable.

Operates in an environment with frequent interruptions, multiple competing priorities, and extensive interaction with faculty, staff, trainees, and institutional partners.

Physical location: Marquam Hill (primary)

Why apply to OHSU?: **We are Oregon's only public academic health center.** In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington. **All are welcome.** OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply. To request reasonable accommodation, contact askhr@ohsu.edu
